Introduce index(i) only after position, then verify with changed examples.
After right or wrong answers, explain in the same chart before a changed retry; arrows are for introduction/correction, not answer-revealing exercise cues.
Introduce k as box width before moving the box with i.
Teach i as box start and move it across changed examples.
Keep the box while introducing sum[i]; too much and too little representation were both rejected.
Compute sum[i] only after box semantics are stable.
Extend the same window update through sum[i+1], sum[i+2], and sum[i+3] with chart validation.
Show the same recurrence repeatedly as i changes rather than jumping straight to a loop.
Explain enumerate(a) in the index/number chart, then probe without revealing the pair and validate in that same chart.
Change only storage form from S[i] = expression to S.append(expression), preserving the RHS and using changed retries when needed.
Bridge algebra into the first Python window-loop pieces before max tracking.
Validation must restore the original array/index/box representation; detached S-only validation was rejected.
Identify which stored S entries contain the current maximum before writing running-max code.
Teach max_sum = S[0] from the first-box value, validate the value, then ask the learner to write the code.
Bridge S[0] to S[i] only because i = 0, without revealing the learner target line.
Only after S[i] production/validation, move to i = 1 and compare the current sum against max_sum.
Have the learner write the comparison with an explicit S[2] index first.
Then generalize the explicit-index comparison to S[i].
Build the max loop from known pieces; dumping the full loop first was rejected.
Combine first-window S creation with max_sum initialization one piece at a time.
Combine later-window S creation with the max comparison after restoring the missing bridge.
Make the obvious if i != 0 case explicit, then explain why else replaces it.
If append conversion is wrong, correct only that relation, retry it, then redo the full else block.
Ground len(a) as array length and connect len(a) - k to the last valid box start.
Then write and verify if i > len(a) - k: break on changed numbers.
Learner detects that the fixed first-window expression does not generalize to arbitrary k.
Reject new window_sum/sum/add vocabulary and retain S as the existing box-sum state.
Introduce range(k), x, and the distinction between j, range(k), and a[k] through discriminator questions.
Do not append per x; initialize one S[i] and update that same storage location as x changes.
A slice/sum built-in detour was introduced then explicitly dropped as premature.
Keep i and k fixed, move x, and show the current S[i] value changing at every inner-loop turn.
Assemble the full combined loop after all pieces are present.
Do not treat final-loop exposure as independent mastery; the learner immediately reports exhaustion.
